s: A SaaS web app runs on EC2 Linux behind an ALB. It stores user sessions in an RDS Multi-AZ database. During high traffic, the app suffers latency due to session read/write. What is the best way to reduce session latency? Options:
o: Store session data in Amazon S3.
Use FSx for Windows and mount it.
Use ElastiCache for Redis to store sessions.
e: Dis the AWS best practice for session storage: Use ElastiCache for Redis— a fast, in-memory data store that handles high throughput with microsecond latency. It's highly scalable, fault-tolerant, and optimized for temporary, fast-access session data. Incorrect: A: S3 is slow and object-based — not for session I/O. B: FSx is Windows-only and not ideal for this use case. C: EBS Multi-Attach has limitations, complexity, and is not suitable for high-performance shared memory. Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/red-ug/WhatIs.html

w.y: Session reads and writes on RDS are causing latency. ElastiCache for Redis is an in-memory store with sub-millisecond latency and is the standard place for web sessions.

o.A: S3 has higher per-request latency than an in-memory store.
o.B: FSx for Windows is a Windows SMB file system, the wrong fit for Linux session storage.
o.C: EBS Multi-Attach is single-AZ and needs a cluster-aware file system.
o.D: Correct: ElastiCache for Redis gives fast, shared session storage.
